correctness.rationale: A connected marked component of order s>=r forces every crossing hyperedge absent but leaves all hyperedges in the complement independent. Because the marked component contains no isolates, its weighted Palm isolate law is exactly I_(n-s). Direct counting of ordered isolated tuples proves all mixed factorial moments, and the covariance follows by subtracting n q^binom(n-1,r-1). Factoring a positive multiplier makes the crossover unique and strict; the log quotient is strictly increasing in s while the binomial-increment mean is nonincreasing. The asymptotic expansions use explicit binomial coefficients and bounded s. The included executable checker independently verifies 44 edge-count/component-size strata in 69,872 enumerated configurations.

originality.rationale: The proposed new part is the exact finite-n fixed-vertex r-uniform hypergraph marked-component deletion law together with the universal, size-monotone sign-crossover hierarchy. Pittel already treats limiting tree-component covariances in ordinary sparse graphs, so their leading r=2 fixed-s case is expressly not claimed novel. Relevant full-text passages on random-graph exploration, hypergraph component exploration, and Poisson-vertex component covariance do not display this package of exact statements. Search absence is only best-knowledge evidence, and older general Palm identities remain a real priority risk.
residual_risks: Pittel (1990) full text inaccessible: stronger finite general formulas may appear in that paper, beyond the abstract.
Classical combinatorial Palm/disintegration arguments can imply the deletion identity implicitly even if the exact hierarchy is not stated.
No claim of independence of scientific review; further literature or human priority review may change originality assessment.

value.rationale: The all-motif, all-component-size classification makes a nontrivial qualitative statement: many structurally different connected component statistics have exactly the same covariance-zero point, and these points are strictly ordered by size. The exact deletion law also supplies arbitrary higher mixed factorial moments, enabling covariance calculations without cataloguing internal hypergraph types. Its endpoint scales interpolate between two natural random-hypergraph transitions, with no assertion that p_* itself is a sharp giant/connectivity threshold.
